title: Persistent Agent Parity with Spawned Agents
note: V1 completed with direct emit. V2 (relay-agent-integration step-5) will migrate to MCP tools for full parity.

summary.goal: Ensure persistent agents (like PlannerLead) function identically to spawned agents from the UI and integration perspective: same status updates emitted to relay, same integration with questions/trajectories system, same visibility in the status bar and agent orchestration UI.
summary.context: PlannerLead runs as a persistent service inside planner-core, connected via RelayClient. This feature established parity via direct emit functions. The relay-agent-integration feature will complete the vision by having PlannerLead use the same MCP tools as spawned agents.

implementation_status.v1_complete: PlannerLead emits agent_joined/status_update/left via direct function calls
implementation_status.v2_pending: relay-agent-integration step-5 will migrate to MCP tools (report_agent_status, ask_user_question)

problem_evidence: Status bar shows '0 agents' even when PlannerLead is active and responding
PlannerLead uses its own conversation-history.ts instead of relay trajectories
useAgentOrchestration.ts listens for agent_status_update messages that PlannerLead never emits
No way for UI to know PlannerLead is 'working' vs 'idle' vs 'needs_input'

acceptance_criteria.description: PlannerLead emits `agent_status_update` messages when its state changes (idle, working, needs_input)
PlannerLead appears in status bar agent avatars section when active
PlannerLead state is visually reflected: green pulse when generating response, idle when waiting
When PlannerLead needs human input (e.g., asks @user a question), it transitions to 'needs_input' state
PlannerLead questions integrate with the question queue system (not just inline chat)
Answers to PlannerLead questions are stored in user trajectory (same as spawned agents)
PlannerLead can query user trajectory before asking questions (deduplication)
Activity popover shows PlannerLead's current activity when clicked
PlannerLead registers itself as an agent on startup (agent_joined event)
PlannerLead unregisters on shutdown (agent_left event)

out_of_scope: Converting PlannerLead to a spawned agent (it remains persistent)
Full trajectory persistence to database (can remain in-memory for v1)
Cross-plan trajectory queries (plan-scoped only for v1)
Multiple persistent agents (only PlannerLead for now)

approaches.name: Emit relay events from PlannerLead (V1 - IMPLEMENTED)
approaches.description: PlannerLead directly emits agent_status_update, agent_joined, agent_left messages via relay. Questions sent via relay protocol same as spawned agents.
pros: UI code needs no changes (already listens for these events)
cons: Persistent and spawned agents use different code paths
Not unified - two ways of doing the same thing

approaches.name: MCP tools as unified interface (V2 - PLANNED)
approaches.description: PlannerLead uses same MCP tools (report_agent_status, ask_user_question) as spawned agents. MCP tools internally call the emit functions.
pros: Truly identical interface for all agents
Single code path for agent→system interaction
cons: Requires MCP tools to be implemented first

summary.approach_rationale: V1 (approach A) is implemented and working. V2 (approach B) is the target state where MCP is the unified interface. relay-agent-integration will implement MCP tools, then step-5 migrates PlannerLead to use them.

notes: Cross-scope contract: Events are broadcast via relay direct messages (not channels) so all connected clients receive them.
AgentState aligns with frontend: 'idle' | 'working' | 'needs_input' | 'error' (frontend 'normal' state is deprecated/unused)

steps.title: Define agent status event types and helpers
steps.description: Create src/relay/agent-status.ts with type definitions and helper functions for emitting standardized agent status events. This establishes the protocol that persistent agents use to broadcast their state.

acceptance_criteria.description: Exports AgentState type: 'idle' | 'working' | 'needs_input' | 'error'
Exports AgentRole type: 'planner-lead' | 'architect' | 'ui-designer' | 'data-modeler' | 'coder' | 'tester' | 'security'
Exports emitAgentJoined() that sends: { type: 'agent_joined', agentId: string, role: AgentRole, displayName: string, state: 'idle', timestamp: string }
Exports emitAgentStatusUpdate() that sends: { type: 'agent_status_update', agentId: string, state: AgentState, activity?: string, step?: string, thought?: string, timestamp: string }
Exports emitAgentLeft() that sends: { type: 'agent_left', agentId: string, reason?: string, timestamp: string }
Events broadcast via sendMessage() to all connected clients (using relay broadcast, not channel-specific)

steps.title: Emit agent_joined on PlannerLead startup
steps.description: Modify planner-lead.ts to emit agent_joined event when PlannerLead connects to relay. This makes PlannerLead visible in the status bar immediately.

acceptance_criteria.description: After successful relay connection and #planner join, emitAgentJoined is called
Agent details include: agentId='PlannerLead', role='planner-lead', displayName='Planning Assistant'
Initial state is 'idle'
On reconnection, agent_joined is re-emitted (relay may have lost presence info)

steps.title: Emit status updates during message handling
steps.description: Modify handleMessage in planner-lead.ts to emit status updates at key points: 'working' when starting to generate response, 'idle' when response sent.

acceptance_criteria.description: When handleMessage starts processing, emit state='working' with activity='Generating response'
If tool use occurs, update activity to 'Using tool: {toolName}'
When response is sent, emit state='idle'
If API error occurs, emit state='error' with activity describing the error
Status updates include channelId context when available

steps.title: Emit agent_left on PlannerLead shutdown
steps.description: Modify stopPlannerLead() to emit agent_left event before disconnecting. This cleanly removes PlannerLead from status bar.

acceptance_criteria.description: stopPlannerLead() emits agent_left before cleanup
Event includes reason='shutdown'
Graceful handling if relay is already disconnected (no error thrown)

steps.title: Update useAgentOrchestration to handle agent_joined/left
steps.description: Extend useAgentOrchestration hook to listen for agent_joined and agent_left events, maintaining the full agent list (not just status updates for existing agents).

acceptance_criteria.description: Add displayName field to Agent interface: { id, role, state, displayName, currentActivity?, currentStep?, currentThought?, hasQuestion }
Update AgentRole type to include 'planner-lead': 'planner-lead' | 'architect' | 'ui-designer' | 'data-modeler' | 'coder' | 'tester' | 'security'
On agent_joined event { type: 'agent_joined', agentId, role, displayName, state }, add new Agent to array
On agent_left event { type: 'agent_left', agentId }, remove Agent from array
Existing agent_status_update handling continues to work (updates existing agent, doesn't create new)

steps.title: Maintain agent registry and broadcast snapshot
steps.description: Maintain in-memory registry of active agents. When a new UI client connects (sends request_agents_snapshot message), respond with agents_snapshot containing all active agents.

acceptance_criteria.description: agent-status.ts maintains Map<agentId, AgentInfo> registry, updated by emitAgentJoined/Left
Exports getActiveAgents() returning [{ agentId, role, displayName, state, activity?, step?, thought? }]
Listen for { type: 'request_agents_snapshot' } message, respond with { type: 'agents_snapshot', agents: [...] }
agents_snapshot shape: { type: 'agents_snapshot', agents: [{ agentId, role, displayName, state, ... }] }

steps.title: Request agents_snapshot on hook mount
steps.description: Modify useAgentOrchestration to request agents_snapshot when mounting (or when relay connects). This ensures UI shows correct state even if it loaded after agents started.

acceptance_criteria.description: On relay connect, send { type: 'request_agents_snapshot' } message via relay
Handle { type: 'agents_snapshot', agents: [...] } response, populate agents array
Map snapshot agents to Agent interface: { id: agentId, role, state, displayName, hasQuestion: state === 'needs_input' }
Subsequent agent_joined/left/status_update events update incrementally

steps.title: Add PlannerLead visual representation in AgentAvatar
steps.description: Update AgentAvatar component to display 'planner-lead' role with appropriate icon/color. Note: AgentRole type update is in pap-005.

acceptance_criteria.description: AgentAvatar has icon mapping for 'planner-lead' role (brain/lightbulb icon or similar)
PlannerLead uses accent-cyan color (matches design system)
Status bar correctly shows PlannerLead avatar with state indicator (green pulse when working, red ring when needs_input)
Tooltip on hover shows displayName ('Planning Assistant')

steps.title: Implement needs_input state for @user questions
steps.description: When PlannerLead detects it needs human input (e.g., generates a question for @user), transition to 'needs_input' state. This triggers the red ring indicator in UI.

acceptance_criteria.description: When response contains @user mention or is a direct question, emit state='needs_input'
Question details included in status update (questionId, questionText preview)
When user responds, transition back to 'working' then 'idle'
needs_input state persists until answered or timeout

steps.title: Integrate with question queue system
steps.description: When PlannerLead asks a question (needs_input), also emit question_added event so it integrates with the question queue UI (not just inline chat).

acceptance_criteria.description: question_added event emitted with: questionId, agentId, questionText, options (if any), priority
Question includes context from conversation history
When answered, emit question_answered event
Question queue UI can display and triage PlannerLead questions same as spawned agent questions

steps.title: Store answers in user trajectory
steps.description: When a PlannerLead question is answered, store the answer in user trajectory format (same as spawned agents). This enables future deduplication.

acceptance_criteria.description: Create src/relay/user-trajectory.ts with QuestionAnsweredEvent type
Store events in memory (Map<planId, UserTrajectoryEvent[]>)
Record: questionId, askingAgent, questionText, selectedOption, reasoning, timestamp
Exports addTrajectoryEvent(planId, event) and getTrajectory(planId) functions

steps.title: Query trajectory before asking questions
steps.description: Before PlannerLead asks a question (adds to queue), check user trajectory for similar past answers. If found, use existing answer instead of asking again.

acceptance_criteria.description: Exports findSimilarAnswer(planId, questionText) that searches trajectory
Simple string similarity check (can be enhanced with embeddings later)
If similar answer found with >0.8 similarity, use that answer
Log when deduplication occurs: 'Using previous answer for similar question'

steps.title: Activity popover data for PlannerLead
steps.description: Include currentActivity, currentStep, and currentThought in status updates so the activity popover has content to display when user clicks PlannerLead avatar.

acceptance_criteria.description: status_update includes activity field (e.g., 'Analyzing plan structure', 'Using tool: read_plan')
When working on specific plan channel (#plan-xxx), include step field with channelId
Optional thought field for 'current thinking' preview (first 100 chars of response being generated)

steps.title: Display activity popover for agents
steps.description: Ensure AgentAvatar activity popover displays currentActivity, currentStep, and currentThought from status updates.

acceptance_criteria.description: Clicking agent avatar opens popover showing: displayName, role, state, currentActivity
If currentThought exists, show truncated preview with 'View full trajectory' link
If agent state is 'error', show error activity in red

steps.title: Write unit tests for agent-status module
steps.description: Create src/relay/agent-status.test.ts with tests for the agent status helpers and registry.

acceptance_criteria.description: Test emitAgentJoined adds to registry and emits event with correct shape
Test emitAgentLeft removes from registry and emits event
Test getActiveAgents returns current registry state
Test request_agents_snapshot triggers agents_snapshot response
Test emitAgentStatusUpdate does NOT affect registry (only broadcasts)

steps.title: Write integration test for PlannerLead visibility
steps.description: Add integration test that verifies PlannerLead emits correct lifecycle events and appears in agents list.

acceptance_criteria.description: Test: initPlannerLead emits agent_joined with agentId='PlannerLead', role='planner-lead'
Test: message handling emits working -> idle sequence
Test: stopPlannerLead emits agent_left
Test: getActiveAgents includes PlannerLead after init, excludes after stop

steps.title: Write tests for useAgentOrchestration hook
steps.description: Add tests for the updated useAgentOrchestration hook to verify it correctly handles agent lifecycle events.

acceptance_criteria.description: Test: agent_joined event adds agent to agents array
Test: agent_left event removes agent from agents array
Test: agents_snapshot populates initial agents
Test: agent_status_update updates existing agent state
Test: 'planner-lead' role is recognized

design_decisions.decision: Emit same events as spawned agents rather than create separate API
design_decisions.rationale: UI already listens for agent_status_update via relay. Emitting the same events means zero UI changes for basic visibility. Consistent protocol for all agent types.
alternatives_considered: SSE stream for persistent agents only

design_decisions.decision: Maintain in-memory agent registry in planner-core
design_decisions.rationale: Needed for agents_snapshot on new connections. Simple Map is sufficient for single persistent agent. Can evolve to SQLite if multi-agent support needed.

design_decisions.decision: Simple string similarity for trajectory deduplication
design_decisions.rationale: MVP approach - more sophisticated semantic matching can be added later with embeddings. For now, exact/near-exact matches are the common case.
